You are a code worker editing the freytag-forge repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files ONLY under the current working directory by RELATIVE paths; NEVER edit anything under the absolute path /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (the main checkout) - a check fails the task if the main checkout changes. Do NOT git commit, do NOT git add -A, do NOT touch .git. Write short notes to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/astra-scoped-vocab2-notes/notes.md (create the directory; this exact path).

OWNED FILES (edit only these): data/stories/continuity-initiative/world.yaml, tests/test_scene_vocabulary_isolation.py (new), tests/test_bench_item_facts.py, tests/test_disclosure_guards.py, tests/test_leak_terms.py, .plans/disclosure-matrix.json, .plans/disclosure-matrix.md (the last two are generated, never hand-edited). Do NOT edit knowledge.yaml, plot.md, pacing.yaml, or any storygame/ code. Read first (read-only): AGENTS.md, docs/world-model-grounding.md (sections on Names and scoped aliases), docs/markdown-story-authoring.md (scoped_aliases), storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py (the entity leak check), tests/test_narration_fixed_thing_terms.py (the validator test pattern), tests/test_scoped_aliases.py.

STEP 0 (baseline): a first attempt produced a patch for items 1, 2 and the new test file. Apply it first from your worktree root with `git apply /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/astra-patches/scoped-vocab.patch` (read-only use of that file) and then continue from that state. That patch left five tests failing and one real offender; your job is to finish it.

PROBLEM: A player command that names a thing from a LATER scene, for example "At the bench her files pointed to, search underneath...", makes the narrator repeat the word, and the narration leak check rejects it with HTTP 409 narration_known_term_leak ("narration mentions an unavailable entity 'bench'"), costing the player a turn. Cause: world.yaml gives the park bench the alias "bench" in `aliases`, and every declared name and alias is guarded in every scene before the thing is nameable. The game must isolate scene-specific vocabulary without errors outside those scenes. The documented fix (docs/world-model-grounding.md) is: keep the specific name guarded and put plain common words in `scoped_aliases`, which name an item only while it is placed and in scene scope.

BUILD:
1. In world.yaml, item `park_bench`: remove the bare alias `bench` from `aliases` (leave `aliases` empty or omit it) and add `scoped_aliases: [bench]`. Keep name `park bench`.
2. Item `storm_drain`: keep `storm-drain` in `aliases`; move `drain` and `tunnel` from `aliases` to `scoped_aliases`.
3. Touch nothing else in world.yaml (the NPC first names and the `hideout` location alias are intentionally left; locations cannot take scoped aliases).

TESTS in the new file tests/test_scene_vocabulary_isolation.py (hermetic, no network; use the pattern of tests/test_narration_fixed_thing_terms.py with NarrationSafetyValidator, RuntimeState, KnowledgeProjector and the continuity-initiative package) with EXACTLY these names:
- test_bare_later_scene_words_do_not_reject_earlier_narration: in scene 1A, narration containing the bare words "bench", "drain" and "tunnel" (for example "She searches under the bench.", "A drain runs along the wall.", "The tunnel is dark.") passes the validator with no ProposalValidationError.
- test_specific_later_scene_names_are_still_guarded_earlier: in scene 1A, narration naming "the park bench" or "the storm drain" is still rejected with code narration_known_term_leak. (If the validator allows one of these in 1A, report it in the notes and assert what it actually does, but do not weaken the check.)
- test_scene_words_still_resolve_in_their_own_scene: in scene 1B with the park bench placed (use apply_scene_placements as tests/test_photo_scoped_alias.py does), the scoped alias resolves "bench" to park_bench via storygame.runtime.knowledge.scoped_alias_entity_ids, and in scene 1A it does not resolve.
- test_guarded_items_have_no_bare_common_word_aliases: for every story package under data/stories (load each with load_story_package), no non-public ITEM has a single-word lowercase entry in `aliases` (such words belong in scoped_aliases). An item whose alias is a single word starting with a capital letter (a proper name) is allowed. List each offender in the assertion message.
FINISH THE JOB (the five remaining failures):
a. world.yaml: item `workstation_chair` keeps its name `workstation chair` but its bare alias `chair` moves to `scoped_aliases` (the new package-wide guard test flags it; later scenes must be able to say "chair"). Check that nothing in the story package or tests breaks because of it.
b. tests/test_bench_item_facts.py::test_park_bench_resolves_and_is_placed_in_scene_1b asserted `world.resolve("bench") == "park_bench"` globally. Keep the test's intent (the park bench resolves and sits in the park in scene 1B): assert `world.resolve("park bench") == "park_bench"` and that `scoped_alias_entity_ids` resolves "bench" to park_bench in scene 1B. Do not change production code.
c. tests/test_disclosure_guards.py::test_public_entity_is_not_a_global_narration_guard used the bare "bench" as the guarded word. Keep its intent (a public item is not a global guard; a legacy one is): use the specific name "The park bench is dusty." in both halves.
d. tests/test_leak_terms.py::test_explicit_leak_term_rejects_before_its_item_is_earned relied on `tunnel` being a global alias. Find out exactly why it now behaves differently, and fix the TEST so it still proves what its name says (an explicit leak term rejects narration before its item is earned) without depending on a bare common-word alias. If the real behaviour of explicit leak terms changed, stop and describe it in the notes instead of papering over it.
e. Regenerate the disclosure matrix with the project script: `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python scripts/disclosure_matrix.py --out-dir .plans` (confirm the flag in the script and tests/test_disclosure_matrix.py), then run tests/test_disclosure_matrix.py. Read the regenerated diff and list in the notes which rows changed and why they are expected (bare words no longer guarded in earlier scenes).
The whole suite must pass, including the new guard test.

HOW TO RUN (the sandbox cannot run uv): from the worktree root, `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_scene_vocabulary_isolation.py tests/test_narration_safety.py tests/test_narration_fixed_thing_terms.py tests/test_scoped_aliases.py tests/test_photo_scoped_alias.py tests/test_leak_terms.py tests/test_knowledge_leakage_matrix.py tests/test_scoped_alias_recall.py tests/test_narration_safety_false_positives.py` then the whole suite: `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov -n 4` (first confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the worktree). Lint: `.../python -m ruff check tests/test_scene_vocabulary_isolation.py` and `-m ruff format`.

HARD RULES: story data, tests and the generated matrix only; no production code changes; no regex over narration; the notes must list files changed, any existing test that needed attention, and any aliases you judged but left alone.
